key_insight: A dependency-aware greedy scheduler can exploit fine-grained parallelism in multi-core quantum circuits and significantly reduce total execution time.
engineering_relevance: For multi-core NISQ systems, better scheduling directly improves core utilization and hides communication latency, making quantum hardware more practical for larger workloads.
method: Baseline: layered scheduling executes all gates in a layer in parallel, then advances sequentially to the next layer.
Proposed: greedy scheduling places each gate as soon as dependencies and resources are ready.
Outcome focus: minimize makespan while improving cross-core utilization and parallel execution.
evidence_signal: On real benchmark circuits, the greedy approach achieved an average 40% reduction in makespan and improved core utilization.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend on accurate dependency tracking and resource availability modeling, which could be challenging on real hardware with noisy communication and limited connectivity.
paper_title: Dependency-Aware Circuit Scheduling for Multi-Core Quantum Systems to Minimize Makespan
